narrative.detail: 0x2BAD8182C09F50c8318d769245beA52C32Be46CD is the LEGITIMATE Arbitrum L1→L2 alias of Uniswap’s real Ethereum-mainnet Governance Timelock (0x1a9C8182C09F50c8318d769245bEA52c32BE35BC) - re-derived by exact arithmetic (alias = L1 address + 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111, mod 2^160, deterministic) and re-confirmed live: the L1 address has real deployed bytecode, the L2 alias has none, which is expected for a bridge alias (a sender identity materialized by the canonical bridge, never itself a deployed contract) - not evidence of vanity-mining or a leaked key. This was previously published here as “vanity-ground to impersonate governance”, which was wrong. It does not mean zero risk: the true authority is Uniswap’s real L1 Governor Bravo + Timelock (DAO vote + a real ~2-day delay), reached via the bridge with no Robinhood-Chain-native control of its own - a different risk shape than a single unprotected key. As of 2026-09-17 this is reflected in the score: 85/100, using the same external-L1-DAO-via-bridge-alias convention already applied to this project’s Base sibling scorer, re-verifying the L1 Timelock’s real 172,800s delay and GovernorBravo’s real 40M-UNI quorum live on every run rather than trusting the correction alone. Added 2026-09-20: this same Timelock is the root of 11 tracked Uniswap targets on 5 ecosystems (Ethereum L1, Arbitrum, Base, Robinhood Chain, Monad), so their cross-exposure reads 80, not 100 (see data/finding_2026-09-20-uniswap-one-timelock-eleven-targets.md).
